before: select waits until a communication case can proceed; if several are ready, it chooses among them rather than honoring source-order priority. A default branch runs only when no communication can proceed immediately.

This fixture places one value in a buffered channel before select, so the receive is ready and default cannot run. The changed fixture leaves the channel empty with no sender, so default runs instead. No time.Sleep or scheduler-order assertion is needed.
Expected output or behavior: 5. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Explain why two ready channels would make a fixed-choice assertion invalid. You may trace it without a Go compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: `select` chooses a channel send or receive that can proceed. If several are ready, their order in the code does not give the first one priority. Without a default, select waits if none is ready.
A `default` branch runs only if no listed channel action can proceed immediately. Here, a value is already waiting in the buffered channel, so the receive is ready.
The screen shows `5`. The receive takes the queued value, so default does not run.
Remove the initial send. The channel is still open but empty, and no sender is ready. default can now run.
